title: Payouts Desk Rule Note: Missing-Pay Credits and Pay Debits on Trips
content:
## The rule

Under **Driver Earnings and Wayfare Pro**:

1. A driver may ask for missing pay on a trip only within the adjustment window: The adjustment window is counted in calendar days from the trip's drop-off or cancellation date: day 1 is the calendar day after it, and the request must be made no later than the last day of the window. The window is 30 calendar days. The trip's own record of its drop-off or cancellation decides the anchor date.
2. Missing pay is credited only when the records show it was owed and not paid:
   - a missing toll reimbursement, when the rider was charged a toll the trip pay left out;
   - missing wait time, when the rider was charged wait time the trip pay left out;
   - a missing cancellation credit, when the rider was charged a cancellation or no-show fee with no driver share posted;
   - a fare correction, when trip pay was computed at the wrong ride option or distance.

   The credit equals what the rules owed less what was paid.
3. A driver's report of time or distance that the trip record does not show is not credited.
4. Support may credit up to 75.00 in total per trip, counting together every support credit already posted on that trip; a request above it is passed to the earnings review team through a policy-not-covered handoff.
5. Debits are posted when a rider charge the driver was paid from is reduced or reversed: a route-inefficiency clawback equal to the rider's fare reduction; a fare correction equal to the reimbursed toll or wait pay that was reversed; a cancellation-fee reversal or cleaning-fee reversal equal to the driver share of what was returned. A debit never exceeds the credit it reverses and may take the balance below zero.

## The window on both sides

| Day of the request, counted from the drop-off or cancellation date | Within the window? |
|---|---|
| The drop-off or cancellation date itself | Yes (the window runs from it) |
| Day 1: the calendar day after that date | Yes |
| Day 30: the last day of the window | Yes |
| Day 31 or later | No |

**Hypothetical dated case.** A trip dropped off on 5 March: day 1 is 6 March and day 30 is 4 April. A request on 4 April is within the window; a request on 5 April is not.

## The support limit on both sides

| Support credits already posted on the trip, plus the credit asked for | Within support's limit? |
|---|---|
| 75.00 or less in total | Yes |
| More than 75.00 in total | No: passed to the earnings review team through a policy-not-covered handoff |

**Hypothetical case.** A trip already carries a support credit of 60.00 for missing wait time. A further missing toll reimbursement of 15.00 brings the trip's support credits to 75.00, within the limit; one of 15.01 would bring them to 75.01, above it.

## Points of judgement

- **What decides "owed"?** The trip record and the rider's charges: a toll or wait time counts only if the rider was charged it; a driver's own account of time or distance the trip record does not show is not credited.
- **How much is credited?** What the rules owed less what was paid. A hypothetical toll of 3.00 charged to the rider with 0.00 reimbursed in trip pay gives a credit of 3.00 at the 100% toll share.
